{{Short description|Algebra concept}}
In [[algebraic topology]], '''homological connectivity''' is a property describing a [[topological space]] based on its [[homology groups]].<ref name=":0" />

== Definitions ==

=== Background ===
''X'' is ''homologically-connected'' if its 0-th homology group equals '''Z''', i.e. <math>H_0(X)\cong \mathbb{Z}</math>, or equivalently, its 0-th [[reduced homology]] group is [[Trivial group|trivial]]: <math>\tilde{H_0}(X)\cong 0</math>.

* For example, when ''X'' is a graph and its set of [[Component (graph theory)|connected components]] is ''C'', <math>H_0(X)\cong \mathbb{Z}^{|C|}</math> and <math>\tilde{H_0}(X)\cong \mathbb{Z}^{|C|-1}</math> (see [[graph homology]]). Therefore, homological connectivity is equivalent to the graph having a single connected component, which is equivalent to [[graph connectivity]]. It is similar to the notion of a [[connected space]].

''X'' is ''homologically 1-connected'' if it is homologically connected, and additionally, its 1-th homology group is trivial, i.e. <math>H_1(X)\cong 0</math>.<ref name=":0" />

* For example, when ''X'' is a connected graph with vertex-set ''V'' and edge-set ''E'', <math>H_1(X) \cong \mathbb{Z}^{|E|-|V|+1}</math>. Therefore, homological 1-connectivity is equivalent to the graph being a [[Tree (graph theory)|tree]]. Informally, it corresponds to ''X'' having no "holes" with a 1-dimensional boundary, which is similar to the notion of a [[simply connected space]].

In general, for any integer ''k'', ''X'' is ''homologically k-connected'' if its reduced homology groups of order 0, 1, ..., ''k'' are all trivial. Note that the reduced homology group equals the homology group for 1,..., ''k'' (only the 0-th reduced homology group is different).

=== Connectivity ===
The ''homological connectivity'' of ''X'', denoted '''conn<sub>H</sub>(X)''', is the largest ''k'' ≥ 0 for which ''X'' is homologically ''k''-connected. Examples:

* If all reduced homology groups of ''X'' are trivial, then '''conn<sub>H</sub>(X) = infinity'''. This holds, for example, for any [[Ball (mathematics)|ball]].
* If the 0th group is trivial but the 1th group is not, then '''conn<sub>H</sub>(X) = 0'''. This holds, for example, for a connected graph with a cycle.
* If all reduced homology groups are non-trivial, then '''conn<sub>H</sub>(X) = -1'''. This holds for any disconnected space.
* The connectivity of the empty space is, by convention, '''conn<sub>H</sub>(X) = -2'''.

Some computations become simpler if the connectivity is defined with an offset of 2, that is, <math>\eta_H(X) := \text{conn}_H(X) + 2</math>.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Aharoni|first1=Ron|last2=Berger|first2=Eli|last3=Kotlar|first3=Dani|last4=Ziv|first4=Ran|date=2017-10-01|title=On a conjecture of Stein|journal=Abhandlungen aus dem Mathematischen Seminar der Universität Hamburg|language=en|volume=87|issue=2|pages=203–211|doi=10.1007/s12188-016-0160-3|s2cid=119139740|issn=1865-8784|arxiv=1605.01982}}</ref> The eta of the empty space is 0, which is its smallest possible value. The eta of any disconnected space is 1.

== Dependence on the field of coefficients ==
The basic definition considers homology groups with integer coefficients. Considering homology groups with other coefficients leads to other definitions of connectivity. For example, ''X'' is ''F<sub>2</sub>-homologically 1-connected'' if its 1st homology group with coefficients from F<sub>2</sub> (the cyclic field of size 2) is trivial, i.e.: <math>H_1(X; \mathbb{F}_2)\cong 0</math>.

== Homological connectivity in specific spaces ==
For homological connectivity of simplicial complexes, see [[simplicial homology]]. Homological connectivity was calculated for various spaces, including:

* The [[independence complex]] of a graph;<ref name=":02">{{Cite journal|last=Meshulam|first=Roy|date=2003-05-01|title=Domination numbers and homology|journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A|volume=102|issue=2|pages=321–330|doi=10.1016/s0097-3165(03)00045-1|issn=0097-3165|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Adamaszek|first1=Michał|last2=Barmak|first2=Jonathan Ariel|date=2011-11-06|title=On a lower bound for the connectivity of the independence complex of a graph|journal=Discrete Mathematics|language=en|volume=311|issue=21|pages=2566–2569|doi=10.1016/j.disc.2011.06.010|issn=0012-365X|doi-access=free}}</ref>
* A random 2-dimensional [[simplicial complex]];<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Linial*|first1=Nathan|last2=Meshulam*|first2=Roy|date=2006-08-01|title=Homological Connectivity Of Random 2-Complexes|journal=Combinatorica|language=en|volume=26|issue=4|pages=475–487|doi=10.1007/s00493-006-0027-9|s2cid=10826092|issn=1439-6912}}</ref>
* A random ''k''-dimensional simplicial complex;<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Meshulam|first1=R.|last2=Wallach|first2=N.|date=2009|title=Homological connectivity of random k-dimensional complexes|journal=Random Structures & Algorithms|language=en|volume=34|issue=3|pages=408–417|doi=10.1002/rsa.20238|issn=1098-2418|arxiv=math/0609773|s2cid=8065082}}</ref>
* A random [[hypergraph]];<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Cooley|first1=Oliver|last2=Haxell|first2=Penny|author2-link=Penny Haxell|last3=Kang|first3=Mihyun|author3-link=Mihyun Kang|last4=Sprüssel|first4=Philipp|date=2016-04-04|title=Homological connectivity of random hypergraphs|class=math.CO|eprint=1604.00842}}</ref>
* A random [[Čech complex]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|last=Bobrowski|first=Omer|date=2019-06-12|title=Homological Connectivity in Random Čech Complexes|class=math.PR|eprint=1906.04861}}</ref>

== Relation with homotopical connectivity ==
[[Hurewicz theorem]] relates the homological connectivity '''<math>\text{conn}_H(X)</math>''' to the [[homotopical connectivity]], denoted by '''<math>\text{conn}_{\pi}(X)</math>'''.

For any ''X'' that is simply-connected, that is, '''<math>\text{conn}_{\pi}(X)\geq 1</math>''', the connectivities are the same:<math display="block">\text{conn}_H(X) = \text{conn}_{\pi}(X)</math>If ''X'' is not simply-connected ('''<math>\text{conn}_{\pi}(X)\leq 0</math>'''), then inequality holds:<math display="block">\text{conn}_H(X)\geq \text{conn}_{\pi}(X)</math>but it may be strict. See [[Homotopical connectivity#homology|Homotopical connectivity]].

== See also ==
'''[[Meshulam's game]]''' is a game played on a graph ''G'', that can be used to calculate a lower bound on the homological connectivity of the independence complex of ''G''.
